title: Fair share: shedding the tenant that is actually over its share
summary: Windowed per-tenant token accounting sheds specifically the tenant using more than its share, and goodput nearly doubles for everyone else.

steps.title: Windowed per-tenant tokens
body: fair_share tracks each tenant's token consumption over a rolling window and sheds admission from whichever tenant is over its fair share, rather than shedding indiscriminately across all tenants.
The comparison run accepts all tenants without any fairness accounting, on the same multi-tenant workload.
steps.look_for: A per-tenant breakdown tile, present here, showing distinct shed rates per tenant.

steps.title: 100% of what is shed comes from the over-share tenant
body: Every request shed under fair_share belongs to the tenant that was consuming more than its share of tokens. No well-behaved tenant is shed to make room.
That is the fairness property this policy is built to demonstrate: the cost of overload lands on whoever caused it.
steps.look_for: The per-tenant shed-rate breakdown: one bar non-zero, the rest at zero.

steps.title: Goodput: 9,157 to 14,496 tok/s
body: Open the A/B view with A = fair_share (this run) and B = accept-all across tenants. Fleet-wide goodput rises from 9,157 tok/s under accept-all to 14,496 tok/s under fair_share — a 58% increase.
The gain is not from doing more work overall; it is from directing the fleet's existing capacity away from a tenant whose excess consumption was producing wasted, unattainable requests for everyone.
steps.look_for: The fleet-wide goodput tile in A against B, and the per-tenant tiles for the well-behaved tenants improving in A.

steps.title: The relationship to per-class SLOs
body: fair_share operates on tenant identity and a token budget, distinct from the priority-and-deadline mechanism in dynamic 7 (mixed SLO classes), though both are forms of the same idea: not all offered load deserves equal claim on scarce capacity.
Whether a fleet needs tenant fairness, class-based admission, or both depends on who the traffic actually comes from.
steps.look_for: The per-tenant goodput tiles for the tenants that were not over their share, before and after switching policy.
